chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr and Ahmad ibn Abi Nasr, in some of their chains, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about making up [prayers] before sunrise and after Asr, so he said, 'Yes, make it up, for it is from the secret of the Family of Muhammad (peace be upon them).'
The Sheikh (may God have mercy on him) said: And it is not permissible to begin voluntary prayers, nor to make up any of them, at the time of sunrise, nor at the time of sunset.

key_terms.سِرِّ آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ: The secret of the Family of Muhammad (implying hidden wisdom or specific jurisprudential nuance)
key_terms.طُلُوعِ الشَّمْسِ: Sunrise (specifically the time when the sun begins to rise, distinct from dawn)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to make up missed prayers before sunrise and after Asr?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib* clarifies the permissibility of performing *qada* (making up) obligatory prayers during *karahah* (disliked) times, distinguishing it from the prohibition of initiating new *nawafil* (voluntary) prayers at sunrise and sunset. Imam al-Sadiq attributes this flexibility to a 'secret of the Family of Muhammad,' highlighting the theological depth behind jurisprudential nuances. The narrator, Al-Sheikh, further refines the ruling by specifying that while *qada* is allowed, starting fresh voluntary prayers is barred during these specific solar transitions.
